requirements.requirement: Run a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: etcd v3.5.17 installed and a fresh 3-member cluster bootstrapped on node1/node2/node3; member list and endpoint health confirm 3 started members; 5 application keys written under /app/config, /app/users, /app/orders and confirmed readable via etcdctl get --prefix.

requirements.requirement: Simulate permanent loss of the node3 member with unrecoverable data
requirements.summary: Keys confirmed present on node3 pre-wipe, then etcd stopped and /var/lib/etcd deleted with rm -rf; ls confirms the data directory no longer exists, directly demonstrating irrecoverable loss of that member's local state.

requirements.requirement: Remove the dead member while quorum is preserved
requirements.summary: etcdctl member remove executed against the surviving node1/node2 endpoints for the dead node3 member ID; resulting member list shows only node1/node2, and both report healthy immediately after removal, showing quorum was never lost.

requirements.requirement: Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node3 system, rejoining the cluster
requirements.summary: etcdctl member add created a new member ID (ed9ba029ee35a4fb, distinct from the original 4df5cadcd9d58187); node3's etcd was reconfigured with --initial-cluster-state existing against a fresh data dir, started, and joined; member list/status show all 3 members healthy with matching raft-applied-index (25).

requirements.requirement: Existing application keys remain intact after the replacement
requirements.summary: etcdctl get /app --prefix issued directly against the new node3 endpoint returns all 5 original key/value pairs unchanged, confirming raft sync restored full data on the replaced member.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre/post restart with changed boot identity and recovered service/cluster/data state
requirements.summary: Boot ID captured before (df8bab0d...) and after (332515f9..., changed) an acknowledged systemctl reboot; post-restart etcd active, 3-member quorum healthy, all app keys present via node1, matching the fixed global boot-identity snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 pre/post restart with changed boot identity and recovered service/cluster/data state
requirements.summary: Boot ID captured before (f7db4b4e...) and after (a239eb9d..., changed) an acknowledged reboot; post-restart etcd active, 3-member quorum healthy, all app keys present via node2, consistent with fixed global snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node3 (replaced member) pre/post restart with changed boot identity and recovered service/cluster/data state
requirements.summary: Boot ID captured pre-replacement/pre-restart (45c22b1f...) and after reboot (218f83b5..., changed); post-restart etcd active, member list shows the replaced member (ed9ba029ee35a4fb) healthy with matching raft-applied-index (39) across all 3 members, and all app keys retrievable from node3.

overall_summary: The executor built a fresh 3-member etcd cluster from scratch (no package was pre-installed), loaded application keys, then faithfully executed the member-replacement runbook: stopped etcd and destroyed node3's data directory to simulate irrecoverable loss, removed the dead member while node1/node2 quorum stayed healthy, added and started a new member on node3 with --initial-cluster-state existing, and confirmed raft sync restored all keys with matching applied-index across all three members. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and evidenced for all three nodes, each showing a distinct pre/post boot ID and full recovery of etcd, quorum, and key data after reboot. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, first-hand command evidence.
limitations: Evidence for the restart protocol relies on the executor's own timeline entries cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots, which is consistent but does not include independent third-party verification.
Minor unnecessary residue (etcd tarball/extracted directory, reboot.log) was left in /tmp on all three nodes; low-severity and does not affect functional correctness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological executor command trace. All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task: etcd binary install (cmd-fa6f349c814944b3, cmd-850035be8a9c4686, cmd-0980dfb658d34577), /etc/hosts and firewalld configuration on all three nodes, systemd unit creation/enable, key writes, the deliberate node3 wipe (cmd-ad5462ba48cb41b0), member remove/add (cmd-2bb9661cc982436f, cmd-cbb3995513de425b), and the three node reboots. No unnecessary experimental mutations, failed troubleshooting side-effects, or weakened security controls were observed; the one failed command (cmd-e71e12cec85e427c, systemd unit startup timeout) was a transient timeout that self-resolved and required no corrective action. The only residue is low-risk build artifacts: the extracted /tmp/etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, /tmp/etcd.tar.gz, and /tmp/reboot.log left behind on all three nodes after installation and reboot, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff. These are bounded, non-sensitive, and do not affect running services, but they were never cleaned up, which is a minor unnecessary-residue deduction.
